cards.b: A fixed-size collection of items of the same data type, each accessed by its index.
Starts at 0. A 5-item array has indices 0 to 4.
An array of arrays: a table with rows and columns, so each item needs two indices.
A data structure made of named fields that can have different data types, e.g. name, age, form.
Array: items all the same type, accessed by index. Record: fields can differ, accessed by field name.
Stores many related values under one name, processed with a loop, so code is shorter and easier to maintain.
Outer loop for rows, inner loop for columns; the inner loop completes for each row.

short.q: Explain why an array is better than 30 separate variables for 30 test marks.
short.model: One array stores all the marks under one name and can be processed with a loop, so the code is much shorter and easier to change.
points: loop can process them / shorter code

short.q: Write Python to print the total of the list marks = [56, 72, 48, 90].
short.model: total = 0 then for m in marks: total = total + m, then print(total) which gives 266.
points: loop adding each item then print

short.q: Write Python to count the letter 'a' in a string word.
short.model: count = 0, then for ch in word: if ch == 'a': count = count + 1, then print(count).

short.q: State the difference between opening a file in write mode and append mode.
short.model: Write mode erases any existing contents of the file before writing. Append mode adds new data to the end and keeps the existing contents.

short.q: A 2D array Seats has 4 rows and 6 columns. Describe how to visit every seat.
short.model: Use a nested loop: an outer loop for rows 0 to 3 and an inner loop for columns 0 to 5, accessing Seats[row, col] each time.
